title: Fidelity Layers & Mini-Handshakes: Hosted API SDK PRD (ideation)
body:
Context / problem statement:
We keep getting signals from SDK users and integrators that the Hosted API surface is powerful but heavy: full session protocols, long-lived sockets, and verbose tool-call scaffolding make simple use cases (single-shot mobile queries, low-bandwidth IoT, or serverless edge functions) awkward. At the same time, larger customers need fine-grained structured output and deterministic tool-call semantics for reliability and safety. The product tension: how do we present a single Hosted API that is both ergonomically simple for tiny clients and expressive enough for production-grade tool orchestration?

This doc sketches an approach: layered fidelity + a "mini-handshake" (compact sessionless/optional session protocol) that allows SDKs and clients to pick a small surface for fast paths and opt into richer features (structured frames, resumability, tool transactions) when needed. Focus is hosted-api + SDK ergonomics (not Dedicated/Dedicated infra details).

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce integration friction for small clients: single-file JS/Go client can make low-latency streaming calls without heavy session management.
- Provide a composable fidelity model (tiny -> standard -> transactional) that maps cleanly to server-side SLOs and routing policies.
- Keep backward compatibility with existing streaming endpoints; make progressive opt-in possible.
- Clear telemetry hooks: per-fidelity metrics, error class breakdown, token and tool call costs.
- Minimal new server infrastructure: leverage existing streaming runtime, add small framing and routing layer.

Non-goals:
- Replacing full session state machine (we keep that for long-lived multi-turn sessions).
- Tackling on-prem deployment packaging for this PRD.

User personas and example flows:
- Mobile chat widget (low bandwidth): wants immediate partial text, no session persistence, occasionally runs a simple tool (search) and can accept approximate results. Picks fidelity="tiny".
- Edge inference in serverless function: single request, wants deterministic JSON output for DB ingestion, may want tool-call side effects within transaction. Picks fidelity="transactional".
- Integrator building orchestration service: wants to stream a long plan, call multiple tools with guaranteed exactly-once semantics and structured frames to reconcile tool outputs. Picks fidelity="standard" or "transactional".

Fidelity model (client-chosen header/query param):
- tiny: minimal handshake, short-lived, opportunistic streaming, no tool transaction guarantees, compact frames (text-first), lower SLO priority (cost-optimized routing).
- standard: full streaming with typed frames, tool-call markers, limited resumability (checkpoint frames), higher SLO priority.
- transactional: explicit tool-call transactions, atomic commit/rollback semantics for tool side effects, strict structured output contract (schema enforcement), highest SLO and audit logging.

Mini-handshake design ideas:
- Client indicates fidelity in a single header (X-Rw-Fidelity: tiny|standard|transactional) or via SDK param.
- For tiny: server accepts a single HTTP/2 or web socket POST with a tiny preface (client-id, request-id, fidelity). No long-lived session. Server streams token deltas prefixed with a 1-byte frame type (text vs control). Tool calls are encoded as a compact control frame with minimal metadata; server returns best-effort tool results (no exactly-once).
- For standard/transactional: server engages a light-weight handshake (exchange of schema/contract pointers, optional can-commit/prepare markers for transactional). Handshake is intentionally short (one roundtrip) so median latency remains low.

Structured output and schema negotiation:
- Clients can include an optional schema URL (or inline schema) in handshake for typed output. Server validates final payload against schema and emits a validation frame if mismatched.
- For tiny fidelity, schema is advisory only: server will try to emit JSON but may send partial text as fallback.
- For transactional fidelity, schema enforcement is required and failed validations cause transaction abort with an explicit error frame.

Tool calling surface (ergonomics):
- Goal: keep tool-calling ergonomics simple for small clients while supporting durable, audited tool transactions for higher fidelity.
- Tiny: tools may be invoked via a simple in-stream control frame: {tool: "search", args: "q:..."}. Response is another compact frame. SDK should expose a helper that turns inline tool calls into local Promises that resolve with best-effort results. No guarantees about dedup or retry.
- Standard: tool calls are represented with ids and call frames; server returns tool-blocking responses (tool output embedded). Limited dedup window via ephemeral idempotency token.
- Transactional: two-phase flow: prepare -> commit/abort. SDK exposes explicit Transaction object with begin/commit/rollback. Server persists transaction log, coordinates exactly-once tool invocation for supported tool adapters.

SDK ergonomics proposals (JS/Go/Python):
- Default high-level API: Redwood.hosted.generate({input, fidelity: 'tiny'}) -> returns AsyncIterable of tokens/fragments. This keeps the common path tiny and stream-friendly.
- Structured helper: Redwood.hosted.structured({schema, input, fidelity}) -> returns final parsed object or throws schema error. SDK should auto-retry parse errors for tiny fidelity based on heuristics.
- Tool helpers:
  - tiny: callInlineTool(name, args) -> returns Promise (best-effort)
  - standard: await callTool(name, args, {idempotencyKey}) -> guaranteed to return server-acknowledged result or explicit error
  - transactional: Transaction.begin(); tx.callTool(...); tx.commit() -> throws on conflicts
- Bundled small footprint client for mobile: single small file that supports tiny path only (no Transaction classes).

Observability / telemetry:
- Add per-request fidelity tag to logs and metrics.
- Track distribution of fidelity choices by client id and SDK version.
- New error classes: schema-validation-failure, transaction-abort, handshake-timeout, tool-timeout.
- Sampling: capture one full debug trace per 1000 tiny calls and one per 100 standard calls to limit overhead.

Backward compatibility and rollout strategy:
- Implement fidelity header as opt-in: default behavior unchanged.
- Start with tiny and standard implementations in a canary region (us-west-2). Route low-risk workloads to tiny path (mobile demos, CI smoke tests).
- Developer preview: SDKs expose fidelity flag behind a beta opt-in. Collect integration feedback.
- Progressive rollout to transactional after end-to-end auditing and a small set of tools implement the exactly-once adapter (search side-effects, DB writes).

Metrics / success criteria:
- Integration time for small clients drops: median time from first draft code to successful stream consumption < 30 minutes in user testing. (measured via partner onboarding surveys)
- 95th percentile end-to-end latency for tiny streaming startup (first token) < 200ms in same-region tests.
- Error rates by fidelity: transactional error rate < 1% after launch (target), schema validation false-positive < 0.1%.
- Uptake: 20% of new SDK installs choose tiny path within 3 months of launch (indicates lowered friction).

Open questions / risks:
- How to price tiny fidelity vs standard? Tiny is cheaper to serve but increases tail-bandwidth patterns. Need finance input.
- Exactly-once semantics for third-party tools: some tool adapters may not be able to support transactional guarantees without adapter changes. Risk: inconsistent guarantees across tool ecosystem.
- Client expectation mismatch: tiny clients may expect the same reliability as standard. Need clear telemetry and docs to surface tradeoffs.
- Security: compact control frames could be misused for injection if parsers are lenient. Need strict encoding rules and XSS-safe SDKs for web.

Implementation notes / engineering sketch:
- Server: add a small framing layer on top of existing streaming runtime. Use a single-byte frame type + length prefix for compact frames to minimize overhead for tiny.
- Routing: fidelity header maps to routing profiles in smart-router (tiny -> low-cost pools, standard/transactional -> higher-priority pools).
- Persistence for transactional: reuse existing durable-logs, but introduce a lightweight transaction coordinator with limited scope (tool-call ordering + commit log).
- SDKs: implement helpers in hosted-api-js repo; mobile client should be tree-shakeable so tiny path has minimal dependencies.

Acceptance criteria for MR/launch checklist:
- API: header/query param accepted and documented, SDK flag documented in quickstart.
- Tiny path: example mobile app uses tiny default and streams tokens with <=200ms first-token median in region tests.
- Standard/transactional: sample integration with search tool and DB write demonstrates prepare/commit flow end-to-end in staging.
- Telemetry: fidelity tag available in console, per-route breakdown in Console UI (beta).
- Security: parsers fuzz-tested, control frames validated, no high-severity findings in internal security review.

Next steps (near-term):
- Product: iterate docs, get pricing projection from finance.
- Eng: spike framing codec and tiny SDK minimal client; prototype in serving-runtime sandbox. (Owner: Marco Li)
- DX: draft quickstart and sample mobile repo using tiny fidelity. (Owner: Nora Williams)
- SRE: compute capacity and routing impacts for tiny workloads.

Notes to self (todo / questions to bring to sync):
- Check whether existing session resume APIs can be reused for standard resumability checkpoints or if transaction semantics need separate endpoints.
- Add examples for fallback behavior when tiny client included schema but server falls back to plain text.
- Wire up a small user study with two partners (startups) to measure integration friction.

---
Revision history:
- 2024-09-10 initial draft (Aisha)
- 2024-10-05 added transactional flow sketch (Marco)
- 2024-11-01 added rollout checklist and acceptance criteria (Aisha)

Feedback wanted: drop-in UX for tiny clients (examples), price delta guidance, risk tolerance for offering mixed guarantees across tool adapters.
